items.excerpt: Google researchers demonstrated a quantum processor that uses reinforcement learning to learn from its own error-correction data mid-computation, continuously recalibrating the hardware without pausing the run. The approach cut logical error rates about 20% beyond conventional calibration and kept performance 3.5x more stable under hardware drift on the Willow chip.

A hybrid quantum-classical AI pipeline designed immune-targeting peptides, with quantum-generated inputs showing particular promise for understudied genetic variants that lack enough data to train classical models alone. It is an early demonstration of quantum-assisted generative modeling feeding real immunology design.

University of Manchester researchers built a physics-informed machine-learning method that screened more than 10,000 candidate 2D materials for rare 'flat-band' electronic states tied to magnetism, unconventional superconductivity and topological behavior. The model confirmed flat-band behavior with 98.2% accuracy, published in Science Advances.

Argonne National Laboratory released ChemGraph, an open-source AI agent framework that automates atomically precise computational-chemistry simulations. It lets researchers without deep computational-chemistry expertise run reliable quantum-chemistry workflows, aiming to translate better simulations into fewer failed experiments for battery, combustion and materials research.

Aalto University researchers used a machine-learning-guided search to identify new kagome-lattice superconductors YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2, narrowing the vast materials space that has to be tested experimentally. The work is part of the broader AI-driven hunt for room-temperature superconductors.

In a PNAS study, TU Dresden researchers combined behavioral experiments with participants' own free-text explanations, analyzed by large language models, to uncover the hidden reasons behind human decisions. It shows LLMs can extract cognitive insight from open-ended text that choice data alone cannot capture, a new tool for cognitive science.

University of Osaka researchers trained an AI model on molecular-dynamics simulations to evaluate 16 competing structural descriptors of supercooled water. The model identified which descriptors best distinguish water's two proposed liquid states, sharpening the decades-old debate over water's liquid-liquid phase transition.
